title: Loop cannot decrease exposure once tag whites clip: target 250 sits on the saturation knee, so the measured ratio collapses to 250/255 and the 0.2-EMA step (0.39%) is swallowed by the 100us write gate -> exposure ratchets up and sticks
claim: With whites clipped at 255 the law `set targetExposureUs [expr {int($currentExposureUs * 250.0 / $denom)}]` / `set nextExposureUs [expr {int(0.8 * $currentExposureUs + 0.2 * $targetExposureUs)}]` (lines 100-101) commands a relative step of only 0.2*(1-250/255) = 0.39% per update, and the gate at line 105 `if {[expr {int($nextExposureUs / 100)}] != [expr {int($currentExposureUs / 100)}]}` drops anything under 100us. A 100us step at w=255 needs cur >= 25,500us, above the 15000 clamp, so the loop can never recover from overexposure anywhere in its range; it only ever moves up (when whites are dim), i.e. it is a ratchet. Separately, 250 is on the clipping knee of the sensor, so the controller aims exactly where the measurement stops responding.
evidence: Pure math (audit/law_math.py): Folk state semantics (state = last written unrounded value, driver truncates to 100us) from 15000 at w=255 -> 14941 -> 14882 -> frozen after 2 writes (driver 14800); at w=253/254 frozen after 1 write; from a user-set 4000 -> 3984 -> frozen. Sim, folk_exact on steady_from_bright (start 20000): 20000 -> 15000 -> 14900 -> 14800 by frame 3, then 14800 for the remaining 19.9 s (margin p10 50.9). Matrix run branch_fast window_drift (ambient 1+0.65 sin, 30 s period): 4000 -> 15000 during the dim phase t=16-22 s, comes back only to 12600 and stays; 0 of 4 tags detected t=32-44 s; repeats each cycle; all_tags 0.805, flicker 34/min. Fine sweep (audit/sweep_fine.txt, steady scene): avgWhite 231 @4000us, 246.6 @4600, 251.2 @4800 (79% of top-quartile samples >=250, 8% at 255), 254.4 @5000 (59% at 255), 255 @5200: between 4000 and 5200 (+30% exposure) the statistic saturates. Detectable range in that scene is 502..~16000us; its log-center (2830us) corresponds to avgWhite ~200, so 200 leaves ~2.5 stops of headroom each way. AprilTag thresholding (vendor/apriltag/apriltag_quad_thresh.c:1181,1197: tile min+(max-min)/2, min_white_black_diff=5) tolerates clipped whites; what kills detection in the sweep is the black level rising with glare/bloom (blacks 195 at 15917us, 219 at 20041 where tags start dropping).
failure_scenario: Room light dims (cloud, evening) -> whites fall below ~222 -> loop raises exposure toward 15000. Light returns -> whites clip at 255 -> law asks for -0.4%/update, gate drops it -> exposure stays at ~12600-15000 forever; every tag's blacks wash out, tags drop in and out (projected elements flash), and the only way out is the user dragging the slider, which the web page disables while AE is on.

verification.reasoning:
Confirmed against the code, pure arithmetic and three targeted simulator runs under Folk state semantics.

Code: autoexposure.folk:75-77 re-reads currentExposureUs with QueryOne! on the Wish the program itself holds (line 107-108), so the state is the last unrounded value written, as the claim assumes. lib/folk.js:323-328 shows the web slider's folk.hold() expands to `Hold! -noncapturing -save -on builtin-programs/web/setup.folk -key {exposure <cam>}`, i.e. the identical key the AE uses, so the AE's Wish replaces the slider's and QueryOne! sees exactly one statement (no 2-result error; the scenario is reachable). camera/usb.folk:329-330 applies `int($exposureTimeUs / 100)` and never re-publishes the truncated value, so no rounding-to-100 feedback exists in Folk.

Math: at avgWhite=255 lines 100-101 give next = cur*(0.8+0.2*250/255) = 0.99608*cur, a -0.39% step; line 105's gate needs a crossing of a 100-bucket, so a step <=50us makes at most one write and a step of 59us (cur=15000) makes two: 15000 -> 14941 -> 14882 then frozen (driver 14800); from a user-set 4000: 4000 -> 3984 then frozen (driver 3900). A guaranteed 100us step needs cur >= 25,500, above the 15,000 clamp at line 103. The fine sweep (audit/sweep_fine.txt) confirms 250 is on the knee: avgWhite 246.6 @4600us -> 255.0 @5200us, with 79% of top-quartile samples >=250 at the target, so the statistic stops responding exactly where the controller aims.

Sim (audit/verify_ratchet.py, cloud_steps 1x->5x->0.2x->1x, Folk semantics, 1-frame cadence): branch tip all_tags 0.664, exposure 4000->3900 frozen through the 5x phase (2/4 tags for 15s), 15000 in the 0.2x phase, then 14800 frozen for the rest of the run, 1047 updates swallowed by the gate. The matrix run branch_fast window_drift also sits at 12600 with 0/4 tags from t=33 to 42s every cycle. The one-token variant (250->200) scores 0.993 and the proposed 5-line fix alone scores 0.998 on the same scenario, so the ratchet is the cause and the fix removes it.

Minor overstatements: (1) "never recover anywhere in its range": between ~12,755 and 15,000 the 50-59us step makes 1-2 bucket crossings before freezing (that is why the sim stops at 12600 and Folk at 14882), functionally the same. (2) "light returns -> tags drop": in the sim at the returned 1x level, 14800us still detects 4/4 tags (steady_from_bright 0.995; cloud_steps t=36-44 4/4) with margin p10 ~44-51 instead of ~94; tags are actually lost on the next brightening (5x: 2/4 tags; window 4x: 0/4), which the loop can never follow. The severity still holds because the controller is one-directional. (3) The window_drift numbers quoted (0.805, 34/min) do not match the current results file (0.721, 42/min); behaviour is identical.
verification.corrected_claim: With tag whites clipped at 255, lines 100-101 command a -0.39% step per update (next = 0.99608*cur) and the 100us write gate at line 105 drops any step that does not cross a 100-bucket, so the loop can only reduce exposure by 1-2 buckets from the very top of its range (>=12,755us) and not at all below that; it is effectively a ratchet that only rises. Target 250 sits on the saturation knee (avgWhite goes 246.6 -> 255 between 4600 and 5200us in the steady sim scene). Consequence: after any dim period raises exposure, the loop stays there; in the sim the stuck level (14800 at 1x) still detects tags with reduced margin, but the loop can never follow any subsequent brightening (5x: 2 of 4 tags for the whole phase; 4x window swing: 0 of 4 tags for ~10s per cycle), and the user cannot intervene because the slider is disabled while AE is on.
verification.fix_assessment: Works as written in Folk/Tcl: the 5-line if/else is valid Jim; pow is a 2-argument expr function (jim.c:9212) compiled in by default (auto.def:423-426; Makefile:103 configures jimtcl without --minimal) and already used by lib/math.tcl:96; `200.0 / $denom` is a double so the double pow path runs; denom >= 1 is guaranteed by lines 98-99, so the ratio is at most 200^2.2 ~ 1.1e5 and cur*ratio fits a 64-bit int even for the web number input's 320000us maximum. No inline comments, no Hold! key change, no new race (body is -serially and the only state is re-read via QueryOne!). The override is continuous with the law at 245 (0.6 vs 0.63) so no chattering at the boundary. Verified standalone (no median, no sweep, no min-step): folk_fixonly cloud_steps all_tags 0.998 vs 0.664 for the tip, min-margin p10 93.7 vs 44.2, 14500 -> 2900 within 1s at 1-frame cadence (at the branch's actual `sleep 5` cadence, jim-signal.c:473-487 confirms seconds, the 8%/update decay would take ~100s, a separate cadence finding). It is not the smallest possible fix: changing the single token 250.0 -> 200.0 already gives a 4.3%/update step at clip and scores 0.993 on cloud_steps (Folk semantics) and 1.000 on window_drift (matrix, sim semantics), though it still stalls below ~2,300us; the 5-line version is better (8% at clip, works down to ~1,250us, gamma-correct gain converges ~2.4x faster from the dark side). The pow 2.2 assumes a gamma-encoded camera as in the sim; on a linear camera the loop gain is 2.2x higher (error multiplier 0.56/update instead of 0.8) but still stable with the 0.2 EMA even with 2 frames of latency. Below ~1,250us the gate still swallows steps, as the claim acknowledges, so the min-step finding is needed for the low end.

title: No recovery path when exposure is so wrong that no tag is detected, and the 1000us floor makes direct sun undetectable in the first place
claim: Lines 70-73 `if {[llength $tags] == 0} { sleep 5; return }` (and 89-92 for statsCount==0) make the loop do nothing exactly when exposure is the reason nothing is detected, and line 102 `if {$nextExposureUs < 1000} { set nextExposureUs 1000 }` forbids the exposures that direct sunlight requires. Combined with finding 1 (loop parks at 12600-15000 when whites clip) a bright spell that drops every tag leaves the camera blind until a human intervenes.
evidence: Single-frame sweep under bright_sun (ambient 30x, audit/sweep.txt): 4 tags detected at <=400us, 3 at 502, 1 at 796, 0 at >=1003us (whites 255, blacks >=243) - the 1000 floor is above the entire detectable range. Steady scene: 0 tags at >=25233us; so any saturated/no-tag state is absorbing. Sim branch_fast on tags_appear_late (start 20000, tags absent 10 s): exposure stays 20000 for the whole no-tag period, then (because the sim scene still detects 3 tags at 20000) drops only to 12600 and sticks. Sim 'fixed' (with the sweep below and floor 300) on bright_sun: 4000 -> 2000 -> 500 -> 400 in 2.1 s, then all 4 tags for the rest (all_tags 0.932). usb.folk:253-271 setExposure does no VIDIOC_QUERYCTRL and FOLK_ENSUREs the ioctl; uvcvideo clamps out-of-range values but other drivers may return EINVAL. web/camera.folk:56-57 slider min=10 (1000us) encodes the same floor.
failure_scenario: Sun hits the table (or the ratchet from finding 1 has parked exposure at 15000 and the light comes back): every tag's blacks wash out, the detector returns an empty list, the AE body returns without touching exposure, forever. Even with tags visible, in direct sun the clamp holds exposure at 1000us where the sweep shows zero detections.
proposed_fix:
Replace lines 70-73 with a halving sweep that wraps, and lower the floor (8 lines):
        if {[llength $tags] == 0} {
            set cur [QueryOne! /someone/ wishes camera $exposureCamera uses exposure time /./ us -default 3000]
            set next [expr {$cur <= 300 ? 15000 : max(300, $cur / 2)}]
            Hold! -on builtin-programs/web/setup.folk -key "exposure $exposureCamera" -save \
                Wish camera $exposureCamera uses exposure time $next us
            sleep 0.5
            return
        }
and line 102 -> `if {$nextExposureUs < 300} { set nextExposureUs 300 }` (also slider min in web/camera.folk:56). A full sweep 15000 -> 300 takes 6 updates (3 s at 0.5 s cadence); tags are picked up at the first detectable step and finding 1's law then converges. Tradeoff to state in the commit: an empty table also sweeps (exposure cycles while no program is on the table). If camera min is a concern, read V4L2_CID_EXPOSURE_ABSOLUTE's minimum once in setExposure (more than 15 lines; not required for the fix).

title: Loop gain ~0.09/update (linear law on gamma-encoded pixels) at a 5 s cadence gives a ~55 s time constant: cannot follow clouds or window light; per-frame cadence would be stable but churns writes
claim: 8-bit pixels go as exposure^(1/2.2), but `int($currentExposureUs * 250.0 / $denom)` (line 100) treats them as linear, so the proportional correction is 1/2.2 of what is needed; after the 0.8/0.2 EMA the small-signal gain per update is 0.2/2.2 = 0.09 in log-exposure, and `sleep 5` (line 111; Jim `sleep` takes seconds) makes one update every ~5 s. Error decays by 1/e in 11 updates = 55 s. From the dark side (w=100) the law asks for x2.5 when x7.5 is needed and the EMA applies x1.3 per update.
evidence: audit/law_math.py: idealized gamma camera, 1000us needing 6000us: 21 updates (105 s at the branch cadence) and it stops at 5000 because the last steps fall under the 100us gate. Sim branch_asis on cloud_steps (ambient 1 -> 5x at 10 s -> 0.2x at 25 s -> 1 at 35 s): exposure 4000 for the whole 5x phase (finding 1; 2 of 4 tags lost for 15 s), then 4000 -> 5000 -> 6000 in 10 s under 0.2x where ~15000 is needed; all_tags 0.667. Matrix branch_asis window_drift: 12 updates in 60 s, exposure 4000..6000 while ambient swings 0.35..1.65. Stability (numeric roots of z^(d+1)-z^d+k): x[n+1]=x[n]-k*x[n-d] is stable for k<1 (d=1 update of actuation delay), k<0.618 (d=2), k<0.445 (d=3). With `sleep 0.5` the 1-3 frame S_CTRL latency is d<1 update, so k=0.2 (law with pow 2.2) is monotone and settles in ~5 updates = 2.5 s; per-frame cadence is d=3 at 30 fps: k=0.2 still stable (21% overshoot), k=0.4 would oscillate (min -0.92). Sim fixed2 (2 Hz cadence, pow 2.2): 3000 -> 600 in 9 s after the 5x step (rate-limited by the 8% clip step), 600 -> 11200 in 5 s after the 0.2x step.
failure_scenario: A cloud passes (3x change in 10 s): the branch moves exposure by ~9% of the remaining error every 5 s, so it is still far off when the light changes back; the user sees exposure 'wander' behind the light, tags dropping in the meantime. With the clip override alone but the 5 s cadence, a 5x recovery would still take ~95 s.
proposed_fix: Use the gamma-correct ratio from finding 1 (`pow(200.0 / $denom, 2.2)`) and change the cadence: line 111 `sleep 5` -> `sleep 0.5` (and the same in the no-tag/deadband early returns). Do not go per-frame: each write is a `Hold! -save` to setup.folk plus a web re-render, and the 100us gate (finding 4) already limits write rate. 2 changed lines.

title: 100us write gate plus re-reading state from the Wish drops sub-quantum steps permanently: error deadband of 500/cur, no decreases, and even the fixed law stalls below ~1250us
claim: `if {[expr {int($nextExposureUs / 100)}] != [expr {int($currentExposureUs / 100)}]} { set currentExposureUs $nextExposureUs ... }` (lines 105-109) only persists the state when a write happens, and line 75-77 re-reads `currentExposureUs` from the Wish each run, so any commanded step smaller than one driver quantum is discarded with no memory. With a 0.2 EMA the condition 0.2*|250/w-1|*cur >= 100 is a deadband on the *error* that scales as 500/cur.
evidence: audit/law_math.py table (worst case cur on a multiple of 100, which is what a user slider sets): cur=1000 no increase unless w<=167; 1500: w<=187; 2000: w<=200; 4000: w<=222; 15000: w<=242; decrease impossible at any cur (needs w>=259-500). Fine sweep: at 4000us the measured step for the observed w=231 is +64us, so the branch does not move at all from a typical setting. Debug run of my first 'fixed' variant (clip step 0.6 under the EMA = 8%/update) under 5x light: state 1196us, whites 255, next = 1100 -> int(1100/100)==int(1196/100) -> no write, stuck at 1100 driver value for 9 s where ~600us was needed (audit/run_fixed__cloud_steps.log shows 1000 flat t=16-25 s; the debug trace prints cur_before=1196 cur_after=1196 every update). The sim's rounding variant stalls the same way at 12600 (branch_fast window_drift/tags_appear_late).
failure_scenario: Bright room, exposure 1000-1500us (bright-day indoor is exactly this range): with the branch law the loop ignores every white value between 187 and 255 and never reduces exposure; with the finding-1 law it still freezes whenever the commanded 8% step is under 100us, i.e. below ~1250us, so the clip override cannot push through.

title: Mean of per-tag whites lets one tag under projector spill or a specular highlight bias all the others; use the median when 3+ tags are visible
claim: `set whiteSum [+ $whiteSum [dict get $stats white]]` (line 85) and `set avgWhite [/ $whiteSum $statsCount]` (line 94) average the top-quartile white over all detected tags. One tag whose top quartile is pinned at 255 by projected light or a highlight shifts the mean by (255-w)/n regardless of the room light, and that tag's value carries no exposure information. Min would instead saturate everyone to lift a shadowed tag; max would chase a spill/highlight down to the floor and, since Folk projects around tags only while they are detected, the spill disappears when the tag is lost (feedback oscillation).
evidence: projector_feedback_mild sweep (15% of tag 1 covered by projector light while detected, audit/sweep_fine.txt): at 4000us detected whites 202/203/203/255 -> mean 216, median 203; at target 200 the mean holds the three unlit tags ~15% darker than intended, and with only two tags visible (255+w)/2=200 puts the unlit tag at 145. Specular sweep (highlight on tag 0): tag 0 clips from 2000us and is lost from 5031us while the other three read 170-232; a mean at the branch target 250 drives exposure to ~5000 and sacrifices tag 0, a median at target 200 sits near 3000 where all four are detected with margins 100-116. Lower bound: per-tag whites in the detectable range span 92..255 (steady sweep), so the median's bias toward the middle tag is safe for detection.
failure_scenario: Two programs on the table plus a bright projected label spilling onto one of them: the spilled tag reads 255, the mean reads (255+w)/2, exposure is driven down until the unlit program is dark (145 at target 200, grey and low-margin), and it flickers; moving the label changes the exposure of every other tag.

title: First version's deadband law limit-cycles through the avgBlack>80 rule; its forced +-100us minimum step is dead code inside the clamp
claim: In v1 (a131ec8b) the branch `} elseif {$avgBlack > 80 && $currentExposureUs > 1000} { set nextExposureUs [expr {int($currentExposureUs * 0.9)}] }` (lines 126-128) fires inside the white deadband [180,240] whenever the black quartile is above 80, and on a real camera the black quartile is ~0.4-0.5 of the white (veiling glare, bloom, JPEG) so it is >80 at every exposure where whites are >=180. That makes the law alternate x0.9 (black rule) and x210/w (white<180 rule): a limit cycle, not the +-100 step. The forced minimum step `if {$nextExposureUs < [+ $currentExposureUs 100]} { set nextExposureUs [+ $currentExposureUs 100] }` (116-118, 122-124) binds only when cur*(210/w-1) < 100, i.e. cur < 600us for w just under 180 (and cur < ~1200us for w just over 240 on the decrease side), so inside the [1000,10000] clamp it never acts.
evidence: Steady-scene whites/blacks from the sweep: white 188 / black 88-108 at 2520us, white 209 / black 97-120 at 3173us, so avgBlack>80 holds across the whole deadband. Analytic iteration (audit/law_math.py, gamma model fitted to the sweep): 4000 -> 3600 -> 3240 -> 2916 -> 2624 -> 2361 -> 2124 -> 2569 -> 2312 -> 2080 -> 2539 -> 2285 -> 2673 ... (period 3-4 updates, +-12%). Sim branch_v1_fast on steady_from_dark: 450 exposure writes in 450 frames, a 12-frame cycle 1800 -> 2100 -> 2600 -> 3400 -> 4100 -> 3700 -> 3300 -> 3000 -> 2700 -> 2400 -> 2200 -> 2000 -> 1800 (+-39%; the 2-frame actuation latency widens it at per-frame cadence). All 4 tags stayed detected (margin p10 83.8) only because the scene is forgiving.
failure_scenario: If v1 is resurrected: steady room light, tags detected, exposure oscillates between ~1800 and ~4100us every 12 frames (or ~+-12% every 15-20 s at the 5 s cadence); the camera preview breathes and tags near either end of the swing flicker.
proposed_fix: Not the tip, so no change is needed on the branch. If the deadband law is brought back: delete the black rule (lines 126-128) or guard it with `$avgWhite > 215` so it cannot fire in the lower half of the white deadband, and delete the four dead minimum-step lines (116-118, 122-124). 1-7 lines.

title: Control law goes blind and freezes once tag whites clip (target 250 ~ saturation); cannot recover from overexposure
claim: With `targetExposureUs = cur * 250 / avgWhite` and 8-bit whites capped at 255, the largest downward correction the law can ever compute while tags are saturated is 250/255 (-2%); after the 0.8/0.2 EMA that is -0.4% per step, and because the wish is never rounded to the camera's 100-us grid (usb.folk:330 applies `int($exposureTimeUs / 100)`), the `int(next/100) != int(cur/100)` deadband stops writing after two steps. So once the tags saturate (sun, cloud clearing, or the ratchet in finding 5) the real system is frozen bright; the simulator (which quantizes commands to 100 us) instead creeps down 100 us per 5 s. Running the same law faster does not help: it rides up to the clip and sticks (sim branch_fast).
failure_scenario: Room goes from shade to sun (or the loop ratchets upward, finding 5): tag whites clip at 255, the AE writes two decrements of ~60 us and then never writes again; the camera stays blown out, tags flicker or vanish, and the only way out is to untick Auto-exposure and drag the slider. In the sim, the branch law needs >20 s (quantized creep) to leave 15000 us; on the real system it never leaves.

title: `sleep 5` is five seconds: 5 s control period with a ~25 s time constant, and sleeping inside the When body ties up a worker and exposes the >100 ms match-kill path
claim: jimtcl's `sleep` takes seconds (vendor/jimtcl/jim-signal.c:472-491: `usleep((int)((t - (int)t) * 1e6)); sleep(t);`), so each AE run blocks for 5 s. The `-serially` prologue (prelude.tcl:559-567 -> __whenOfCurrentMatchIncompleteChildMatchesCount, folk.c:602-621 -> db.c:561-578) keeps counting the sleeping match even after its parent detection statement is removed one frame later, because matchAcquire only checks `gen`, not `alive` (db.c:50-64); every detection statement that arrives meanwhile (2 per frame: both detectors match the pattern) spawns a match that returns in the prologue. Effective period = 5 s + <=1 frame; with the 0.2 EMA the loop time constant is ~25 s, far slower than window/cloud changes. Side effects: one of the cpuUsableCount-1 workers (folk.c:1754) sleeps 5 s per cycle, and the gray frame is pinned for 5 s via inherited destructors. The kill path in matchRemoveSelf (db.c:874-892: SIGUSR1 if the match is incomplete and has run >100 ms wall-clock, clockid=CLOCK_MONOTONIC folk.c:1501, ns per common.h:70-76) does not fire today only because the parent statement is removed within one frame; it would fire every cycle (JIM_SIGNAL -> workerExit -> thread exit and respawn with a full interpreter boot, folk.c:960-963, 1517-1540, 1636-1637) if the parent lived longer, e.g. camera <10 fps or the `-keep` fix in finding 3.
failure_scenario: Blinds open or a cloud passes (light changes over 5-30 s): the AE updates once every 5 s by 20% of the error, so the picture stays too dark/bright for 20-30 s after every change and tags drop out meanwhile. On a camera running below 10 fps, or after finding 3's fix, the sleeping body is SIGUSR1-killed every cycle and a worker thread is torn down and re-booted each time.
proposed_fix:
Do not sleep in the body; rate-limit with a held timestamp. Insert after line 67 (`if {[lindex $detector 1] ne "entire-frame"} { return }`):
```
        set nowMs [clock milliseconds]
        set lastRunMs [QueryOne! camera $camera autoexposure last ran at /./ ms -default 0]
        if {$nowMs - $lastRunMs < 250} { return }
        Hold! -key [list lastRan $camera] \
            Claim camera $camera autoexposure last ran at $nowMs ms
```
and delete the three `sleep 5` lines (71, 90, 111). Net +5/-3 lines; every run then completes in milliseconds, so no worker is held, no frame is pinned, and the >100 ms kill path cannot hit the AE. 250 ms exceeds the V4L2 actuator latency (1-3 frames). Minimal alternative: change the three lines to `sleep 0.25` (3 lines) but keep the kill caveat above.

title: Detection Claims are silently dropped whenever entire-frame detection takes longer than one camera frame (Hold! removal in 1f0595f2), so AE never fires and detection jitters on slower machines
claim: On the branch the gray frame is a plain child Claim of the jpeg-frame match, and the jpeg Hold! is replaced every frame (usb.folk:360-362; 60 fps requested at usb.folk:141). Replacing the hold removes the old jpeg statement immediately (folk.c:262-268 -> statementDecrParentCountAndMaybeRemoveSelf), which removes the decode match and the gray-frame statement (db.c:653-658, 700-711) and calls matchRemoveSelf on the entire-frame detector match, setting its childStatements to CHILD_STATEMENTS_REMOVING (db.c:862-868). When the still-running detector then does `Claim [list $this entire-frame] detects tags ...` (apriltags.folk:133-134), Say -> dbInsertOrReuseStatement aborts because the parent match is being removed (db.c:1221-1233; Say returns STATEMENT_REF_NULL, folk.c:314-358). So a detection statement exists only if jpeg->gray decode plus detection finishes inside ~16.7 ms. On main both the gray frame and the detections were `Hold!`-ed (main usb.folk:281, apriltags.folk:133, 205), which is global and immune to the match removal.
evidence:
branch usb.folk:281-282:
```
        Claim camera $cameraPath has gray frame $grayImage at timestamp $ts \
            -destructor [list $imageLib imageFree $grayImage]
```
branch apriltags.folk:123-124, 133-134:
```
When /nobody/ wishes to calibrate camera /any/ to display /any/ /...etc/ &\
    -serially camera /camera/ has gray frame /frame/ at timestamp /frameTs/ {
    ...
        Claim [list $this entire-frame] detects tags $tags on camera $camera \
            at timestamp $frameTs with time $aprilTime grayFrame $frame
```
usb.folk:360-362: `Hold! -key [list camera $camera jpeg] Claim camera $camera has jpeg frame $jpeg at timestamp $timestamp -destructor ...`. db.c:1221-1233: `if (cs == NULL || cs == CHILD_STATEMENTS_REMOVING) { ... clauseFree(clause); return NULL; }`. The tip commit message itself says the goal is to "work even on systems where AprilTag detection is really slow (so gray frame statement gets invalidated right now before we can autoexposure)"; the AE When only accepts entire-frame detections (autoexposure.folk:67).
failure_scenario: 1280x720 or 1080p camera on a Raspberry Pi or a busy laptop: entire-frame detection takes 30-150 ms, so every entire-frame detection Claim is aborted; only the incremental detector (which needs earlier detections and must also finish within a frame) sometimes succeeds. Tags flicker, newly placed tags are never discovered, and the AE body never runs at all. Users see 'detection jitters' and an AE checkbox that does nothing.
proposed_fix: One line, usb.folk:281: `Claim -keep 300ms camera $cameraPath has gray frame $grayImage at timestamp $ts \`. `-keep` defers removal via sysmon (prelude.tcl:403-410 parses it; db.c:620-636 schedules; sysmon.c:296-310 fires; already used by `Claim -keep 8ms` at apriltags.folk:238), so the detector match stays live 300 ms past the next jpeg, the detection Claim succeeds, and the carried `grayFrame` stays valid through destructor inheritance. Cost: up to 300 ms x fps gray frames pinned (about 36 MB at 1080p/60 fps) and tag-removal latency grows by <=300 ms in the collector. K must exceed worst-case decode+detection on the target hardware (use 500ms on a Pi), otherwise the >100 ms kill path (db.c:874-892) hits the detector worker; pair with finding 2 so the AE body is never the long-running incomplete match. Do NOT instead restore `Hold!` on the detection Claims: a held statement has no parent match and inherits no destructors (folk.c:230-270, dbHoldStatement), so its `grayFrame $frame` would point at freed memory once the gray statement and its matches are gone.

title: AE assumes 3000 us at startup while the camera is still in its V4L2 boot (auto) state; first write is computed from a wrong baseline, and the manual slider is absent on a fresh system
claim: `QueryOne! ... uses exposure time /./ us -default 3000` reports 3000 when nobody has wished an exposure, but usb.folk only calls setExposure from `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time /exposureTimeUs/ us` (usb.folk:329-331) and nothing wishes one at boot unless a saved hold exists (save-holds.folk:149-168). The camera is therefore in whatever mode it booted in (UVC cameras default to aperture-priority auto). The first AE write is 0.8*3000 + 0.2*(3000*250/white), i.e. 3000-4000 us regardless of the real exposure, so the picture jumps; with the 5 s period the loop then needs ~8-10 cycles (40-50 s) to converge. title: Bottom-quartile 'black' is biased by tag code; sample the guaranteed-black ring outside the quad instead

title: Branch removed the Hold! on gray/RGB frame claims: every new jpeg tears down the gray frame, the detector match and the tag detections before the next frame is decoded/detected (per-frame gap -> flashing)

Combined with the same removal in apriltags.folk (branch:133-134, 202-203 are plain Claims; main:133 and :203 were `Hold! -key [list $this entire-frame]` / `incremental`), each frame now destroys gray frame -> detector match -> `detects tags` claims immediately, while the replacement chain only exists after decode+detect of the new frame. On each frame the previous `tag $id has detection` statements expire 8 ms after the jpeg swap, and the new ones appear only after decode+detect, so every tag is 'undetected' for (decode+detect-8) ms on every single frame. Everything keyed on tag detection (program outlines, projected regions, calibration overlays) is torn down and rebuilt at frame rate with a gap whose length depends on detection time, i.e. on lighting -- exactly 'projected elements flash rapidly depending on lighting' and 'detection jitters'. Because a held statement does not inherit its match's destructors, the raw `grayFrame $frame` pointer must not ride on a held detection claim: delete `grayFrame $frame` from both detection claims (apriltags.folk:134, 203) and make the AE join the live frame instead -- autoexposure.folk:65-66 becomes `When -serially /detector/ detects tags /tags/ on camera $camera at timestamp /frameTs/ with /...options/ & camera $camera has gray frame /frame/ at timestamp /any/ {` and delete line 68 `set frame [dict get $options grayFrame]` (the match inherits the gray statement's destructor, so the image stays alive for the body). ~13 changed lines across three files. Caveat for the AE lens: db.c:968-983 SIGUSR1-kills any body still running >100 ms after a parent statement is replaced, so the AE body must not `sleep` at frame-rate-replaced inputs regardless of which fix is taken.

Conversely, if someone raises the constant to 30000 on a camera that really runs 60 fps, the camera drops to ~30 fps and tracking latency doubles.

The AE's `currentExposureUs` is `QueryOne! /someone/ wishes camera ... -default 3000` (autoexposure.folk:63, 75-77), so until a wish exists the multiplicative law `cur*250/white` is anchored at 3000 regardless of reality.

The camera's own AE had settled at ~20 ms with a decent image; the first Folk AE step commands ~3.6 ms, the picture goes almost black, and with the branch's 5 s cadence it takes ~9 acting steps (~45 s) to climb back to the cap; on a real webcam (noisier than the simulator at 3.6 ms) tags can disappear entirely, and since `if {[llength $tags] == 0} { sleep 5; return }` never adjusts exposure, the AE is then stuck dark until the user drags the (disabled) slider or restarts.

In runCamera after the warm-up loop (line 317) add `set exposureNow [$camLib getExposure $camObj]` / `if {$exposureNow > 0} {` / `Hold! -key [list camera $camera exposure] \` / `Claim camera $camera has exposure time [expr {$exposureNow * 100}] us` / `}`. autoexposure.folk:77 `-default 3000` -> `-default [QueryOne! camera $exposureCamera has exposure time /./ us -default 3000]`. 11 lines. (UVC GET_CUR of exposure_time_absolute reports the live auto value on Logitech-class cameras, so the first step starts from reality; cameras without the control return -1 and keep today's behaviour.)

title: setExposure fires-and-forgets: errors only become a `camera/usb.folk has error` claim on another thread (never the retry loop), out-of-range values are silently clamped by uvcvideo, and the applied value returned in c.value is discarded -- AE belief and camera state diverge with no signal
claim: Error path: FOLK_ENSURE is `Jim_SetResultString(...); longjmp(__onError, 0)` (lib/c.tcl:97) -> the C wrapper returns JIM_ERR -> a Tcl error inside the exposure When body (usb.folk:329-331), which runs on a different worker than the frame loop (see notes). prelude.tcl:182-197 evaluateBlock catches it, prints `Error while running $this` and does `Say -nonatomically $this has error $err with info $opts`; runWhenBlock (folk.c:873-1003) completes the match. Nothing reaches runCamera's `try` (usb.folk:371-384), so the camera keeps streaming with the old exposure and NO reopen happens. Range: uvcvideo's uvc_ctrl_set -> uvc_ctrl_clamp rounds INTEGER controls to GET_RES and clamps to [GET_MIN, GET_MAX] without error, and v4l_s_ctrl copies the applied value back (`p->value = ctrl.value`), but setExposure returns void. A missing control or a MANUAL mode absent from the camera's menu mask returns -EINVAL -> error claim on every AE step. Folk never issues VIDIOC_QUERYCTRL, so the web slider's 10..48 and the AE's 1000..15000 are guesses.
evidence: usb.folk:253-271: `$camc proc setExposure {Camera* camera int value} void {` ... `c.id = V4L2_CID_EXPOSURE_ABSOLUTE; c.value = value; FOLK_ENSURE(xioctl(camera->fd, VIDIOC_S_CTRL, &c) == 0);` (c.value is never read back). usb.folk:329-331 `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time /exposureTimeUs/ us { $camLib setExposure $camObj [expr {int($exposureTimeUs / 100)}] }`. prelude.tcl:184-195 `} on error {err opts} { ... Say -nonatomically $this has error $err with info $opts }`. Kernel (torvalds master, fetched): uvc_ctrl.c `value = min + DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST((u32)(value - min), step) * step;` then `clamp_t(u32, value, min, max)`; `if (!ctrl) return -EINVAL;`; menu `if (!test_bit(value, &mapping->menu_mask)) return -EINVAL;`. v4l2-ioctl.c v4l_s_ctrl: `ret = ops->vidioc_s_ext_ctrls(file, NULL, &ctrls); p->value = ctrl.value; return ret;`. Calibrate page sample: `exposure_time_absolute ... min=3 max=2047 step=1` (C920-class); other UVC cameras expose e.g. min=50 (5 ms).
failure_scenario: (a) Camera whose exposure_time_absolute minimum is 50 (5 ms): AE wishes 1000 us, the kernel applies 5 ms and returns 50 in c.value which is dropped; the AE's `cur` is the wish (1000), so `target = 1000*250/255` -> next clamps at 1000 -> the AE reports itself converged while the tags are washed out and nothing in the UI shows the camera is really at 5 ms. (b) Camera without a MANUAL exposure mode or without the control (some Microsoft/laptop UVC cams, v4l2loopback): every AE update (each 5 s) raises `builtin-programs/camera/usb.folk has error assertion failed: xioctl(...) == 0`; the camera keeps running on its own auto exposure, and the AE keeps 'adjusting' a value that never reaches the hardware. Also note any wish below 100 us maps to value 0 and silently switches the camera to aperture-priority auto (line 257-260).
proposed_fix: Return and claim the applied value. usb.folk:253 `$camc proc setExposure {Camera* camera int value} int {`; add `int applied = 0;` after line 254; after the EXPOSURE_ABSOLUTE S_CTRL (line 269) add `applied = c.value;` and `if (applied != value) fprintf(stderr, "setExposure: camera clamped %d -> %d\n", value, applied);`; replace the closing of the proc with `return applied;` (returns 0 in the auto branch). usb.folk:329-331 body becomes `set applied [$camLib setExposure $camObj [expr {int($exposureTimeUs / 100)}]]` / `Hold! -key [list camera $camera exposure] \` / `Claim camera $camera has exposure time [expr {$applied * 100}] us`. AE consumer (autoexposure.folk:75-77): `set currentExposureUs [QueryOne! camera $exposureCamera has exposure time /./ us -default $currentExposureUs]` so the law multiplies the real exposure. ~10 lines. Follow-up (>15 lines, separate): a `queryExposureRange` proc doing VIDIOC_QUERYCTRL on V4L2_CID_EXPOSURE_ABSOLUTE and claiming `camera $camera has exposure range min/max/step` so the AE and the /camera slider clamp to the camera instead of 10..48 / 1000..15000.

title: Exposure When is re-declared inside runCamera on every retry-loop reopen; the previous one (capturing the free()d Camera*) is never removed -> duplicate ioctls per Wish change and a latent use-after-free
claim: `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time ...` (usb.folk:329-331) captures `$camObj` by value (captureEnvStack, prelude.tcl:93+; the code itself says `HACK: we don't capture upvars yet`, line 309) and is a child statement of the camera program's match. The outer retry loop (usb.folk:369-389) calls runCamera again inside the *same* match after an error, so a second When with the new pointer is added while the first one -- whose Camera struct was free()d by cameraClose (line 101) -- stays alive (db.c matchRemoveSelf 922-966 only removes children when a parent statement goes, which never happens here). Each reopen adds one more stale handler. Threading itself is fine: the body runs on another worker (Say pushes to the worker's queue, folk.c:76-82/203-210; idle workers steal, folk.c:1472-1515) but uvcvideo sets `vdev->lock = &queue->mutex` so the v4l2 core serializes S_CTRL against DQBUF/QBUF/poll.
evidence: usb.folk:329-331 `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time /exposureTimeUs/ us { $camLib setExposure $camObj [expr {int($exposureTimeUs / 100)}] }` declared inside `fn runCamera` (line 304); usb.folk:369-389 `while true { set camObj {}; try -signal { runCamera camObj } on error e { puts stderr "camera/usb: Error $e" } ... finally { if {$camObj ne {}} { ... $camLib cameraClose $camObj } }; sleep 1 }`; cameraClose ends with `free(camera);` (line 101). Commit 8664c12f 'Fixes to make retry loop work (even on unplug-replug)' shows the reopen path is exercised in practice. No Retract/unhold of the When exists anywhere (grep prelude.tcl).
failure_scenario: Camera hiccup (select timeout x5, unplug/replug, EBUSY): runCamera errors, cameraClose frees the struct, 1 s later a new Camera is malloc'd (glibc's per-thread tcache usually hands back the very same chunk, which is why this mostly 'works'). From then on every AE/slider Wish change runs N+1 setExposure bodies: N stale ones dereference freed memory (UB; if the chunk was reused by something else the ioctl hits a garbage fd -> EBADF/ENOTTY -> `camera/usb.folk has error`), plus the duplicate USB control transfers each hold the queue mutex and stall the frame loop. After several reopens the user sees spurious error claims on the camera program and growing frame-time spikes whenever the AE moves.
proposed_fix: Give the handler a key so a reopen replaces it. usb.folk:329-331 -> `Hold! -key [list camera $camera exposure-control] {` / `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time /exposureTimeUs/ us {` / `$camLib setExposure $camObj [expr {int($exposureTimeUs / 100)}]` / `}` / `}` (Hold! body form creates a pattern-less `when` whose child When dies when the hold is replaced, prelude.tcl:355-365, folk.c:1197-1201). In the retry loop's `finally` (line 379), before cameraClose, add `Hold! -key [list camera $camera exposure-control] ""` so no handler outlives the camera on the signal/termination path (empty clause removes the hold, prelude.tcl:349-351). 3 changed lines. Alternative (12 lines) that also moves the ioctl onto the frame-loop thread: drop the When and, once per frame, `Query! /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses exposure time /exposureTimeUs/ us`, calling setExposure inside a `try ... on error` only when the value differs from the last applied one.

title: No second actuator: Folk never touches V4L2_CID_GAIN, so once exposure hits the frame-interval cap the AE has nothing left for low light
claim: setExposure (usb.folk:253-271) is the only control Folk sets (`grep -n GAIN builtin-programs lib` -> nothing). uvcvideo maps V4L2_CID_GAIN to UVC PU_GAIN_CONTROL (unsigned 16-bit INTEGER; Logitech C920-class 0..255, see the calibrate page's sample `gain 0x00980913 (int) : min=0 max=255`). Not every camera has it, so a setter must tolerate -EINVAL instead of FOLK_ENSURE-ing.
evidence: usb.folk:253 `$camc proc setExposure {Camera* camera int value} void {` is the only VIDIOC_S_CTRL user; calibrate-page.folk:225 sample output `gain 0x00980913 (int) : min=0 max=255 step=1 default=0 value=109`; kernel uvc_ctrl.c mapping `V4L2_CID_GAIN ... UVC_GUID_UVC_PROCESSING, UVC_PU_GAIN_CONTROL, size 16, V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_INTEGER` (fetched). Sim very_dark: at the 15 ms cap all_tags_rate 0.007 (driver_lens_b_hi15000.json) -- that is the regime where a gain step would be the only remaining move once the interval cap is honoured.
failure_scenario: Camera really at 60 fps (cap 15 ms) in a dark room: AE pins exposure at the cap, white stays ~60-90, tags flicker, and the AE has no further action; meanwhile the camera's own gain (which its built-in AE would have raised) is left wherever the last process set it -- sometimes 0 after a replug, sometimes 109 from a previous auto session, so the same room gives different results across restarts.
proposed_fix: usb.folk, after setExposure: `$camc proc setGain {Camera* camera int value} int {` / `struct v4l2_control c = { .id = V4L2_CID_GAIN, .value = value };` / `if (xioctl(camera->fd, VIDIOC_S_CTRL, &c) == -1) { perror("camera/usb: setGain"); return -1; }` / `return c.value;` / `}` and next to the exposure handler: `When /someone/ wishes camera $camera uses gain /gain/ {` / `$camLib setGain $camObj $gain` / `}` (inside the same Hold! block as finding 5). 8 lines in the driver. AE side (other lens, ~6 lines): only when nextExposureUs equals the cap and avgWhite is still below target, `Wish camera $exposureCamera uses gain G` stepping G up by 16 (0..255), and wish gain 0 whenever exposure is below the cap, so gain is the last resort (it amplifies noise and lowers AprilTag decode margin). Do this after the frame-interval cap (finding 2), which recovers most low-light cases without noise.
